name: Zach Lipson
current_role: Investor/advisor, Lightweight Ventures (former co-founder & Chief Product Officer, Dutchie)
profile: Serial entrepreneur who co-founded Dutchie in 2017 with his younger brother Ross; as chief product officer he helped build it into the leading cannabis e-commerce/point-of-sale platform (valued ~$3.75B in 2021). The brothers left Dutchie in early 2023; he has since invested in and advised early-stage startups.
interesting_fact: Dutchie started in Bend, Oregon; within two years it served 450 dispensaries in 18 states and was pitched as 'a Shopify of the cannabis space maybe meets DoorDash'. Ross described Zach as the methodical one: 'Zach is the one who wants to make sure that we're doing everything right.'
notes: No longer at Dutchie (left Feb 2023; the founders later filed suit against company leadership, so avoid framing outreach around Dutchie's current management). Low public profile; LinkedIn is the likely route. Appeared on the 'To Be Blunt' cannabis podcast (ep. 020).

name: Sammy Krikler
current_role: Co-founder, Chief Insurance Officer and board member, Earnix
profile: Israeli statistician and co-founder (2001) of Earnix, whose AI-driven pricing and rating software is used by insurers and banks to price policies and loans. He is the only one of the three co-founders still at the company, which became a unicorn in 2021 after a $75M round led by Insight Partners.
interesting_fact: Earnix's CEO Udi Ziv has called Krikler 'the brains of the product'; of the three 2001 co-founders (with Yoni Cheifetz and Shai Fogel) he is the one who stayed for two decades-plus.
notes: Very low media profile. Aggregator profiles say he studied statistics at the Hebrew University and was R&D manager at Eventus Software before Earnix (unverified primary source). Route via Earnix press/marketing or LinkedIn.

name: Laurent Ritter
profile: French entrepreneur who co-founded Paris mobile-game publisher Voodoo with Alexandre Yazdi in 2013. Voodoo became a hyper-casual gaming giant (Goldman Sachs and Tencent invested) and was valued around $2B. Ritter is also an active angel investor in European startups.
interesting_fact: Voodoo, which he co-founded in 2013, grew from a small Paris studio into one of the world's most-downloaded mobile game publishers, popularising 'hyper-casual' games.
notes: Low public profile; Yazdi is Voodoo's public face (CEO). Investor databases describe Ritter as an ESC Rennes alumnus who runs an angel vehicle called Purple (not verified from a primary source). Current operational role at Voodoo unclear.

name: Felipe Delgado
current_role: Co-founder (CFO/President), Merama; partner and board member, Beetmann Energy
profile: Mexican finance executive who co-founded Merama in 2020, a Mexico City/São Paulo group that acquires and scales leading Latin American e-commerce brands; its 2022 Series B valued it at $1.2B. Before that he was CEO/CFO of Beetmann, a Mexican wholesale-electricity supplier and renewable-energy developer using AI/IoT to optimise energy use.
interesting_fact: He has an energy background unusual for an e-commerce founder: he ran Beetmann Energy, a qualified supplier in Mexico's wholesale electricity market that develops renewable plants, and remains a partner and board member there.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career in J.P. Morgan's US Oil & Gas investment-banking group, holds a UT Austin BBA (Walter B. Smith Scholar) and a Harvard MBA, and is a keen runner who has completed two marathons; Quién named him a 'Titan of Business' among its 50 people transforming Mexico (2022).
notes: Strong energy-podcast angle via Beetmann. Titles vary by source (CFO vs President). Low media profile; LinkedIn or Merama is the route.

name: Jordan Feldman
profile: Harvard-educated former Goldman Sachs banker who co-founded Rightway (c.2017), a New York healthcare-navigation and pharmacy-benefits company combining clinician-led support with an app to help members find high-quality, cost-efficient care. Rightway reached a unicorn valuation and Feldman remains CEO.
interesting_fact: He co-founded Rightway with his father, physician Dr. Theodore Feldman (its chief medical officer); his father's experience as a doctor inspired the clinician-led model.
deep_cut_fact: Before healthcare he worked on Goldman Sachs' Mortgage Trading and Investment Banking teams, then left to help found RedBird Capital Partners, Gerry Cardinale's private-equity firm; he holds an A.B. in Government and Economics from Harvard.
notes: Speaks at Conference Board events; reachable via Rightway's press/marketing team or LinkedIn.

name: Dave Merkel
current_role: Co-founder and board member, Expel (stepped down as CEO Nov 2026; succeeded by Steve Kelley)
profile: Cybersecurity veteran who co-founded Herndon, VA managed detection-and-response firm Expel in 2016 with Yanek Korff and Justin Bajko and led it as CEO for a decade to a $1B+ valuation. Previously CTO of Mandiant and then FireEye after their 2014 merger. In November 2026 he handed the CEO role to Steve Kelley and stayed on the board.
interesting_fact: Expel's founders said they started it because they couldn't buy the security service they wanted: 'a few practitioners left to build the service they wished they could buy.'
deep_cut_fact: He started his ~30-year security career as a federal agent investigating cybercriminals (other bios specify the US Air Force Office of Special Investigations); his own author bio jokes that he is often mistaken for Willy Wonka.
notes: Just transitioned out of the CEO seat (GovInfoSecurity, 10 Nov 2026) -> may have more time for a podcast. Frequent RSA Conference speaker; blogs on expel.com.

name: Thomas Jonas
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Nature's Fynd (now The Fynder Group), Chicago
profile: French-born HEC graduate and former packaging-industry executive (MeadWestvaco beauty & personal care, Alcan Beauty Solutions) who co-founded Nature's Fynd around 2014. The Chicago company grows 'Fy', a protein from a fungus first studied in NASA-funded Yellowstone extremophile research, via fermentation; it raised ~$500M from backers including Bill Gates' Breakthrough Energy and was valued at ~$1B.
interesting_fact: The company's microbe comes from Yellowstone's volcanic hot springs, discovered by co-founder Mark Kozubal during NASA-funded research into how life might survive on other planets.
deep_cut_fact: After HEC (class of 1993) he served as a French Air Force officer and then ran a European-food distribution business in Hong Kong; his pivot to sustainability came in 2012 when a family holiday on Kaua'i stretched to a year and he saw plastic bottles piling up on the beaches. HEC named him 'HEC of the Year' 2022.
notes: Company rebranded from Nature's Fynd to The Fynder Group (food, pharma, materials). Has done climate podcasts before (My Climate Journey ep.169) - receptive to podcast format. Quote: 'It is not by lecturing and making people feel guilty that we will have an impact on the world.'

name: Linhao Zhang
current_role: Co-founder, Formation Bio (stepped back from CTO role Aug 2025)
profile: Software engineer (UT Austin computer science; ex-Salesforce and Oscar Health) who in 2016 co-founded TrialSpark with Benjamine Liu and Kit Dobyns to fix the clinical-trial bottleneck. TrialSpark evolved from trial software into a full CRO and then an AI-native drug developer, rebranding as Formation Bio in Dec 2023 (backed by a16z, Sequoia, Thrive). Zhang served as CTO until Aug 2025 and remains a co-founder.
interesting_fact: TrialSpark began because co-founder Liu, as an Oxford doctoral student, found pharma companies turning away promising Parkinson's drug candidates simply for lack of trial capacity; the company now in-licenses and develops drugs itself using AI.
deep_cut_fact: He and co-founder Kit Dobyns first met as roommates during a Salesforce internship.
notes: Low public profile; CEO Benjamine Liu is the company's public face. Some profiles list him as COO from 2021; Contrary says he left the CTO post Aug 2025. Best route LinkedIn.

name: Le Hong Minh
current_role: Founder and Chairman, VNG Corporation (Vietnam); founding a new AI venture for non-desk workers
profile: Born 1977, Monash-educated (finance) former PwC and VinaCapital staffer who founded Vinagame in 2004 with 15bn VND; it became VNG, Vietnam's first tech unicorn, behind online games, Zalo messenger and ZaloPay. CEO 2004-2024, he became chairman again in Nov 2024 and is VNG's largest individual shareholder. In 2025 he began building AI tools for Southeast Asia's non-desk workforce.
interesting_fact: He estimates 60-80% of Vietnam's workforce never sits behind a computer, which is the market for his new AI venture 'for the 80 percent'.
deep_cut_fact: A former hardcore gamer who says he could play nonstop for 48 hours, he still goes to the office daily two decades on and trains ~10 hours a week for triathlons 'as a reminder of discipline'. He judges character by how someone treats a waiter.
notes: Name in input given as 'Hong Minh'; full name Le Hong Minh (Lê Hồng Minh). VNG also builds AI/cloud data-center infrastructure in Vietnam (relevant for data-center podcast). Route via VNG corporate communications.

name: Aaron DeBevoise
profile: YouTube-economy pioneer (name spelled DeBevoise; input has 'DeBovoise') who co-built gaming network Machinima (EVP Network Programming, 2007-13) and fashion network StyleHaul, then founded Spotter in 2019. Spotter licenses creators' back catalogs for upfront cash (MrBeast, Dude Perfect and many others) and has grown into a creator studio/ads/AI-tools company valued at ~$1.7B.
interesting_fact: Spotter has deployed close to $800 million to YouTubers ranging from MrBeast to Aaron 'AB' Brown and Kinigra Deon, and was named a TIME100 Most Influential Company.
deep_cut_fact: Before Spotter he helped build two of YouTube's earliest multi-channel networks: gaming network Machinima, where he ran network programming and orchestrated show deals, and the fashion/beauty network StyleHaul. LA Business Journal named him to its LA500 in 2024.

public_contacts.value: Guest on Colossus 'Business Breakdowns' EP.78 (Spotter: Funding YouTube Creators)

notes: Frequent podcast guest (Business Breakdowns, Foundr) - comfortable with the format. Route via Spotter communications.

name: Akin Babayigit
current_role: Co-founder and board member, Tripledot Studios; partner, Arcadia Gaming Advisors ($100M mobile-games fund)
profile: Games executive and Harvard MBA who co-founded London-based Tripledot Studios (Solitaire, Woodoku, etc.) and served as its president/COO for about seven years before stepping back in Sept 2024; he remains on the board. Previously at Facebook and King. In 2025 he launched Arcadia Gaming Advisors with a ~$100M fund for mobile-game studios.
interesting_fact: Bloomberg dubbed him a mobile gaming 'kingpin' when he launched a $100 million fund to back mobile-game developers; he is an early investor in Turkish studios such as Dream Games and Spyke Games.
deep_cut_fact: He spent nearly five years at Facebook, where he led games partnerships in Europe and was one of the people who launched the Facebook Audience Network, before heading business operations & special projects at King; he also co-founded playable-ads company Luna Labs.
notes: Well connected in the Istanbul games scene. No published contact found; LinkedIn or via Tripledot/Arcadia. Tripledot acquired AppLovin's apps business in 2025.

name: Itai Damti
profile: Israeli fintech operator who co-founded brokerage-tech provider Leverate (grew to ~160 staff without VC money) and later ran its Asia-Pacific business from Hong Kong. In 2019 he and Doron Somech founded Unit, an embedded-finance/banking-as-a-service platform letting companies launch accounts, cards and lending 'in weeks, not years'; it became a unicorn in 2022 ($100M Series C led by Insight).
interesting_fact: He and CTO Doron Somech had both left Leverate in 2015-16 and reunited about three years later to start Unit, which hit a $1.2B valuation within roughly three years.
deep_cut_fact: Before Unit he was a Fintech Entrepreneur in Residence at 500 Startups and EIR at hardware accelerator HAX, and is a special advisor to Hong Kong investment bank Ion Pacific; he has written guest columns for TechCrunch.
notes: Active writer/speaker on embedded finance. Route via Unit marketing/press or LinkedIn.

name: Sam Teller
profile: Listed by Hurun as a FabFitFun founder, but FabFitFun's documented co-founders are Daniel Broukhim, Michael Broukhim and Katie Rosen Kitchens; only one aggregator profile (zerogtalent) adds a 'Sam Teller', with no detail. Could not confirm who this person is or his role.
notes: Likely a data error in the source list. Do not confuse with the better-known Sam Teller (Elon Musk's former chief of staff, Astera Institute founder) - no link to FabFitFun found. Recommend dropping or verifying via FabFitFun directly.

name: Arik Liberzon
current_role: Founder and board member, Pentera (formerly co-founder & CTO)
profile: Israeli cyber-warfare veteran (Dr. Arik Liberzon) who co-founded Pcysys, now Pentera, in 2015 to turn offensive-security expertise into software. Pentera's automated penetration-testing / security-validation platform became a unicorn in 2022 (backers include Insight, Blackstone, K1, Evolution). Amitai Ratzon is CEO; Liberzon served as CTO and now sits on the board as founder.
interesting_fact: Pentera's platform automates what human 'ethical hackers' do, safely running real attack techniques against a company's own network to validate which exposures are actually exploitable; CEO Amitai Ratzon joined Liberzon while the company was still in stealth mode.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Pentera he headed the Cyber Warfare group in the Israeli military's Computer Service Directorate, a unit with experience in both defensive and offensive cyber.
notes: Very low public profile; CEO Amitai Ratzon does most media. Pentera's About page lists him as 'Dr. Arik Liberzon, Founder' under Board Members.

name: Michael Otte
current_role: Early co-founder/technical contributor, Freenome (current role unknown)
profile: Listed in some company profiles as one of four people (with his brother Gabriel Otte, Charlie Roberts and Riley Ennis) who launched Freenome in South San Francisco in 2014. Freenome develops blood tests that use machine learning on cell-free DNA and other biomarkers for early cancer detection. Most founder accounts name only three co-founders; his current role could not be confirmed.
interesting_fact: In Freenome's 2015 seed announcement (a16z-led $5.55M), co-founder Gabriel Otte thanked his brother Michael Otte as 'instrumental in the development of the Freenome technology'.
notes: Very little public information; founder status contested (BioSpace quotes Ennis naming three founders). Not to be confused with brother Gabriel Otte (former Freenome CEO). Verify before outreach.
